mu_name_from: MuMain's ZzzOpenData.cpp loads the group as MODEL_SWORD + i from Sword{i+1}, so Sword07.bmd is index 6, which OpenMU's 0.75 table names the Gladius. MuWeapons.cs agrees from the client's side: `new("Gladius", "Sword07.bmd", WeaponStance.Sword, ...)`.
why_this_one: Hanzo's counter is the last shop in Lorencia with lines that do not resolve, and this is one of them. A shelf drops what it cannot draw - shared/Market builds the row and leaves out anything whose group and number find no asset - so the blacksmith sold ten of his twenty-four lines and the rest of the counter was empty air. This one is the exception and it is worth naming: the Gladius and the Falchion are both given slot 73 in OpenMU's own store, so the second wins and the Gladius never reaches the shelf. It is built anyway - it is drop level 20 and drops_from_monsters is true, so it falls in the world whether or not Hanzo stocks it, and shared/Market's remarks explain why the collision is kept rather than tidied.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Weapons.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: CreateWeapon(group, number, slot, skillNumber, width, height, dropsFromMonsters, name, dropLevel, minimumDamage, maximumDamage, attackSpeed, durability, magicPower, levelRequirement, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, energyRequirement, vitalityRequirement, wizardClass, knightClass, elfClass).
stats.width_note: Width is where OpenMU keeps two-handedness - `if (group < Bows && width == 2)` - and one here agrees with MuWeapons.cs's TwoHanded: false. It is also what takes a fifth off the price: shared/Market.Coin reads the footprint's width to tell a one-handed weapon from a two-handed one.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are the wizard, knight and elf flags, and MuWeapons.cs carries the same set from the client's side.
stats.skill_note: The skillNumber of the call. There are no skills in this simulation, so it is carried for the row to read against the call it came from and nothing more - and it is the reason this item is dearer in the original than the price MU2 charges, since OpenMU multiplies a skilled item's price by two and a half. See shared/Market's remarks.

stance_from: MuWeapons.cs: WeaponStance.Sword, TwoHanded: false. Actions 4 and 17, the family the Kris, the Short Sword and the Hand Axe already walk in. A one-handed blade leaves the shield hand free, which is the whole point of it on a counter that is mostly shields.
sheet_from: Data/Item/sword08.OZJ (128x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names sword08.jpg; 66 triangles, one mesh.
material_note:
The brightest sheet in the batch and the easiest to read. Island 0 is the blade, twelve triangles from Z 13 to 135, at (212, 206, 183) chroma 29 - a white blade with gold filigree laid along it. Steel: the filigree is a small part of a large bright surface, and it is colour rather than a different surface.

Island 2 is the crossguard, twenty-eight triangles in four units of Z, at (191, 155, 73) and chroma 118 - the strongest colour reading of any weapon island here. That is gold and nothing else, so brass.

Island 1 is the grip at (101, 85, 48) chroma 53, dark bands with the gold pommel at the end. leather_wrap.
